checklist.step: Inventory every document that constitutes the written information-security program
actions: In the GRC platform open Policy Management ▸ Policy Register and filter Category = 'Information Security'.
List every policy, standard and procedure claimed as part of the WISP: cyber risk policy, acceptable use, access control, encryption, incident response, vendor security, data classification.
For each, record owner, version, last approval date and next review date on the WISP inventory worksheet.
Flag any document with an approval older than 12 months and hand the flag list to the Chief Info Security Officer.
File the inventory worksheet in the compliance evidence repository under WISP/<review-year>.
checklist.done: the inventory lists every WISP document with owner, version and approval date, and stale documents are flagged.

checklist.step: Map each Cyber Code and Insurance Code section to a WISP control
actions: Download the current Insurance Sector Operational Cyber Risk Management Code of Conduct and the Insurance Code of Conduct (August 2022) from the BMA website (bma.bm ▸ Legislation & Guidance) and date-stamp the captures.
Build a two-column mapping matrix: each code section (governance, risk assessment, technical controls, incident response, outsourcing, 3LOD) against the WISP document and section that satisfies it.
Mark any code section with no mapped control as a GAP row with a proposed owner.
Load the matrix into the GRC platform as the compliance mapping for the Bermuda cyber obligation and link each row to the policy record.
checklist.done: every code section maps to a named WISP section or carries an owned GAP row, with dated source captures on file.

checklist.step: Refresh the information-asset and critical-service scope behind the program
actions: In the CMDB run the report of applications and infrastructure tagged Criticality = 'Critical' or handling policyholder personal information.
Reconcile the report against the prior year's WISP scope statement and list additions and retirements.
Ask the Business Continuity Manager for the current critical-services register and align the WISP scope to it.
Update the WISP scope appendix with the reconciled asset and service list and the reconciliation date.
checklist.done: the WISP scope appendix matches the current CMDB critical-asset list and the critical-services register.

checklist.step: Draft the year's WISP updates from gap rows, incidents and threat changes
actions: Collect inputs: GAP rows from the mapping matrix, the year's incident post-mortems from the Incident Response Lead, penetration-test findings, and any new BMA guidance notes.
Redline each affected WISP document, keeping section numbering stable so the code mapping survives.
Route redlines to the named document owners for technical review with a 10-business-day turnaround.
Log every accepted and rejected change in the document version history.
checklist.done: every gap, post-mortem action and guidance change is either redlined into a WISP document or logged as rejected with a reason.

checklist.step: Run the proportionality assessment against the insurer's class and risk profile
actions: Record the entity's BMA registration class (e.g. Class 4 / Class E) from the certificate of registration.
Assess whether the program's depth matches the nature, scale and complexity test in the Insurance Code of Conduct s.4 proportionality principle, and write the rationale.
Where the program exceeds or trails the class expectation, note the justification (group standards, US state overlays) in the WISP governance section.
File the proportionality memo with the review-year evidence.
checklist.done: a dated proportionality memo ties the program's depth to the entity's registration class and risk profile.

checklist.step: Obtain legal review of the code mapping and self-report criteria
actions: Re-read the 'consequences of non-compliance' section of the Insurance Code of Conduct (August 2022) and confirm the WISP's materiality criteria for BMA self-reports still align with it.
Review the mapping matrix rows marked GAP and advise which gaps are reportable weaknesses versus improvement items.
Confirm the self-report template contains the failure description, root cause, remediation plan and target dates the BMA expects.
Return written comments to the Security GRC Analyst within 10 business days.
checklist.done: counsel has confirmed the materiality criteria and self-report template in writing, with gap classifications recorded.

checklist.step: Present the refreshed program to the board and obtain approval
actions: Prepare the annual CISO report: program changes, incident summary, risk assessment results, gap remediation status and the proportionality memo.
Upload the report and the redlined cyber risk policy to the board portal meeting pack at least 7 days before the meeting.
Present at the board (or delegated risk committee) meeting and take the approval resolution for the cyber risk policy and WISP updates.
Obtain the minute extract from the Corporate Secretary and attach it to the policy records in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: the board minute extract approving the cyber risk policy and WISP updates is attached to the policy records.

checklist.step: Publish the approved WISP and collect staff attestations
actions: Publish the approved document versions to the intranet policy library, superseding the prior versions with effective dates.
In the learning management system assign the annual security-policy attestation campaign to all staff and contractors, due in 30 days.
Chase non-completers weekly via their line managers; escalate over-30-day non-completion to the Chief HR Officer.
Export the completion report and file it with the review-year evidence.
checklist.done: approved versions are live, and the attestation completion report shows 100% or documented escalations.

checklist.step: Arm the next annual review cycle in the GRC calendar
actions: In the GRC platform create the next-cycle review task dated T-120 days before the target board approval date.
Configure T-60 and T-30 escalation reminders to the Chief Info Security Officer and Corporate Secretary.
Link the task to the WISP inventory so a new document added mid-year inherits the review date.
Verify the reminder fired correctly for the current cycle and note any calendar defect.
checklist.done: the next review task exists with T-120/T-60/T-30 reminders wired to named recipients.

checklist.step: Maintain the materiality criteria for reporting failures to the BMA
actions: Document the tests that make a compliance failure material: policyholder harm, prudential impact, systemic control breakdown, regulatory deadline missed, or matters informing the BMA's sound-and-prudent-conduct assessment.
Set the decision rule: any failure meeting a test goes to the BMA self-report workflow; borderline cases go to Regulatory Counsel within 5 business days.
Publish the criteria in the compliance manual and brief the Compliance Officer team at the quarterly meeting.
Review the criteria whenever the BMA issues new guidance on the Code.
checklist.done: written materiality criteria with a decision rule and escalation path are published in the compliance manual.

checklist.step: Assess every identified failure against the materiality criteria
actions: On each new breach-log entry, complete the materiality assessment form: which criteria were tested, evidence considered, and the material / not-material conclusion.
Timestamp the determination date — it starts the self-report clock for material failures.
Route material determinations to the Head of Compliance for sign-off the same day.
Record not-material rationales in full; a bare 'not material' conclusion is rejected at QA.
checklist.done: every breach-log entry carries a timestamped, evidenced materiality determination signed where material.

checklist.step: Self-report material failures to the BMA with a remediation plan
actions: Draft the self-report using the counsel-approved template: failure description, code sections affected, root cause, customer/prudential impact, remediation actions with owners and dates.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the draft before anything is sent to the Authority.
Submit to the entity's BMA supervisory contact through the established correspondence channel and request written acknowledgment.
File the sent report and the BMA acknowledgment in the compliance evidence repository, and link both to the breach-log entry.
checklist.done: the cleared self-report is with the BMA, acknowledgment is on file, and the breach-log entry links to both.

checklist.step: Track self-reported remediation through to closure
actions: Load each remediation action from the self-report into the GRC action tracker with owner and committed date.
Review progress monthly; any action forecast to miss its committed date triggers a written update to the Head of Compliance for onward BMA notification.
Collect closure evidence (changed configuration, revised procedure, retraining records) before marking an action complete.
Report open self-report actions to the risk committee quarterly.
checklist.done: every self-reported action is tracked to an evidenced closure or a notified date change.

checklist.step: Log program waivers and exceptions with disposition
actions: Record every approved deviation from a WISP requirement as an exception record: requirement, business reason, compensating control, expiry date, approver.
Cap exception duration at 12 months; renewal requires a fresh risk assessment.
Run the monthly expired-exception report and chase owners for closure or renewal.
Include the open-exception count in the CISO's annual board report.
checklist.done: no WISP deviation exists outside a dated, approved, compensated exception record.

checklist.step: Retain the review-cycle evidence for the retention period
actions: Assemble the cycle bundle: WISP inventory, mapping matrix with dated code captures, proportionality memo, counsel comments, board minute extract, attestation report, breach log extract and any self-reports.
File the bundle in the compliance evidence repository under entity/WISP/<review-year> with the 10-year retention label.
Verify the repository index returns the bundle by entity and year before closing the cycle task.
checklist.done: the complete cycle bundle is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by entity and year.

testing.step: Build the population of WISP documents, approvals and failures for the period
actions: Extract from the GRC policy register every document tagged to the WISP, with version and approval dates.
Extract the full breach log and exception log for the audit period.
Pull the board and risk-committee minutes list from the Corporate Secretary for the same period.
Sign the extract as the test population with the extraction date and row counts.
testing.done: a signed population of documents, log entries and minutes exists with row counts recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the document population to the intranet policy library
actions: Compare the GRC register list to the documents actually published in the intranet policy library.
List documents published but not registered, and registered but not published — both are completeness exceptions.
Confirm the published version number matches the register's approved version for every WISP document.
Resolve or log every difference before sampling.
testing.done: register and library agree on document set and versions, or differences are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Re-perform the Cyber Code mapping on a sample of sections
actions: Select 10 sections of the Cyber Code spanning governance, risk assessment, technical controls, incident response and outsourcing.
Read each section from the current BMA-published text and independently identify which WISP control should satisfy it, before looking at the mapping matrix.
Compare to the matrix; a mapping to a control that does not actually address the section text is an exception.
Capture the code text relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled section has an independent mapping note that agrees with the matrix or a logged exception.

testing.step: Verify board approval is current and properly minuted
actions: Open the board portal meeting pack for the approval meeting and confirm the CISO report and redlined cyber risk policy were in the pack.
Read the minute extract and confirm the resolution names the cyber risk policy and WISP updates approved.
Check the approval date falls within 12 months of the prior approval.
Confirm the minute extract is attached to the GRC policy records.
testing.done: a minuted board approval within the 12-month window is evidenced in both the portal and the GRC records.

testing.step: Recompute the review-cycle date maths
actions: For each WISP document, compute months elapsed between the two most recent approvals.
Flag any interval over 12 months as a late review, and check whether a logged exception covered it.
Verify the next-cycle T-120/T-60/T-30 reminders exist in the GRC calendar and address named current staff.
testing.done: every document shows a ≤12-month approval interval or a covering exception, and next-cycle reminders are armed.

testing.step: Trace breach-log entries to materiality determinations
actions: Take 100% of breach-log entries marked material and a random sample of 15 marked not-material.
Confirm each carries a completed, timestamped materiality assessment naming the criteria tested.
For the not-material sample, independently re-apply the criteria; a determination you would overturn is an exception.
Confirm material determinations carry the Head of Compliance sign-off.
testing.done: all material entries and the not-material sample carry defensible, signed, timestamped determinations.

testing.step: Verify every material failure produced a cleared BMA self-report
actions: For each material determination, locate the self-report, the counsel clearance record and the BMA acknowledgment.
Check the report content covers failure, root cause, impact and dated remediation plan.
Confirm the report went to the Authority promptly after the determination date; an unexplained lag over 10 business days is an exception.
A material failure with no self-report is a reportable finding to the Audit Committee, not a workpaper note.
testing.done: every material failure traces to a cleared, acknowledged self-report sent promptly after determination.

testing.step: Test staff attestation completion
actions: Export the attestation campaign report from the learning management system for the period.
Reconcile the assignee list to the HR active-headcount report to prove the campaign reached everyone.
Sample 10 completions and verify the attestation names the current policy version.
List non-completers without a documented escalation as exceptions.
testing.done: campaign coverage reconciles to headcount and sampled attestations reference the current version.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a ticket per exception with the document or log entry reference, what failed and the code section affected.
Assign a root cause (stale document, mapping error, missed determination, unreported failure) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date; unreported-material-failure exceptions open an immediate self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has a ticket, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance thresholds for unmapped sections and unreported material failures.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references.
Sign as independent reviewer, having authored no WISP document or determination in the period.
Report the result to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Fix the assessment scope from the CMDB and critical-services register
actions: Run the CMDB report of all applications, databases and infrastructure tagged Criticality = 'Critical' or holding policyholder personal information.
Merge in the Business Continuity Manager's critical-services register so every critical service maps to its supporting assets.
Compare to last year's scope; list additions and removals with reasons.
Have the Chief Info Security Officer sign the scope statement before any scoring starts.
checklist.done: a signed scope statement covers every critical asset and service, with year-on-year changes explained.

checklist.step: Refresh the threat catalogue for the insurance-specific landscape
actions: Update the threat catalogue from the year's SIEM incident data, FS-ISAC advisories and BMA sector communications.
Add or re-weight scenarios: ransomware on the policy admin platform, data exfiltration of policyholder PII, vendor compromise, DDoS on customer portals, payment-redirection fraud.
Map each threat scenario to the asset classes it targets so scoring inherits the right threat set.
Publish the catalogue version used for this cycle into Archer.
checklist.done: a versioned threat catalogue, updated from live incident and sector data, is loaded for scoring.

checklist.step: Run authenticated vulnerability scans across the scoped estate
actions: In the scanner console verify the asset groups match the signed scope statement; add any missing hosts before launching.
Launch authenticated scans with the current plugin/signature set and confirm credentialed coverage above 95% of targets.
Export the findings report with CVSS scores and asset mappings.
Hand the export to the Security GRC Analyst for scoring input and file it with the cycle evidence.
checklist.done: authenticated scan results covering ≥95% of scoped assets are exported and filed.

checklist.step: Commission and review the annual penetration test
actions: Agree the test scope with the IT Security Manager: external perimeter, customer portal, and one internal lateral-movement scenario against the policy admin environment.
Execute the test under the signed rules of engagement and document every finding with reproduction steps and severity.
Debrief the Cybersecurity Lead within 5 business days of test completion.
Deliver the final report and load each finding into the Archer finding register.
checklist.done: the pentest report is delivered and every finding is registered with severity and reproduction steps.

checklist.step: Assess vendor-hosted critical services
actions: From the vendor inventory, list every third party hosting or processing a scoped critical service or policyholder data.
Collect each vendor's current SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 evidence and map exceptions in those reports to the insurer's risk register.
Score vendor-side residual risk with the same 5x5 scale used internally.
Feed vendor risk rows into the enterprise assessment so hosted services are not scored as risk-free.
checklist.done: every vendor-hosted critical service carries a residual score grounded in current assurance reports.

checklist.step: Score inherent risk per asset class against the threat catalogue
actions: In Archer open Risk Management ▸ Assessments and create the cycle's assessment instance linked to the signed scope.
For each asset-class/threat pair, score likelihood and impact on the methodology's 5x5 scale, citing scan data, incident history and threat weighting.
Record the evidence reference behind every score — unsupported scores are rejected at review.
Generate the inherent-risk heat map draft.
checklist.done: every asset-class/threat pair carries an evidenced inherent score in the Archer assessment instance.

checklist.step: Evaluate control effectiveness against each scored risk
actions: For each high or critical inherent risk, list the operating controls (MFA, EDR, segmentation, backups, monitoring) that mitigate it.
Rate each control's design and operating effectiveness using the year's control-test results, not aspiration.
Downgrade any control with an open critical finding or failed test to 'partially effective'.
Record the control ratings in Archer against the risk rows.
checklist.done: every high/critical risk carries control ratings backed by actual test results.

checklist.step: Compute residual risk and compare to appetite
actions: Apply the methodology's residual formula to each risk row and generate the residual heat map.
Compare each residual score to the board-approved cyber risk appetite thresholds.
List every out-of-appetite risk with its driver (control gap, unpatched estate, vendor exposure).
Send the out-of-appetite list to the Chief Risk Officer and Chief Info Security Officer the same week.
checklist.done: a residual heat map exists and every out-of-appetite risk is listed with its driver and notified.

checklist.step: Build the prioritised remediation plan
checklist.by: Vulnerability Management Lead / Security Engineering Lead
checklist.role: Vulnerability Management Lead / Security Engineering Lead
actions: Convert each finding into a ServiceNow remediation ticket with severity-driven due dates: critical 30 days, high 90 days, medium 180 days.
Assign each ticket a named engineering owner, not a queue.
Bundle related findings into remediation projects where one fix (e.g. a patching campaign) closes many rows.
Publish the plan summary to the Chief Info Security Officer with the count and age profile by severity.
checklist.done: every finding has an owned, dated ticket and the plan summary is with the CISO.

checklist.step: Capture risk acceptances for anything that will stay out of appetite
actions: For each out-of-appetite risk not remediable within SLA, require a written acceptance memo: business reason, compensating controls, exposure period, review date.
Sign or reject each memo; rejected items go back for accelerated remediation funding.
Cap acceptance periods at 12 months with mandatory re-assessment.
Log signed acceptances in Archer linked to the risk rows.
checklist.done: no out-of-appetite risk exists without a signed, time-boxed acceptance memo or an accelerated plan.

checklist.step: Present the assessment to the board or risk committee
actions: Prepare the assessment pack: methodology recap, coverage statement, residual heat map, top-10 risks, remediation plan and acceptance register.
Upload to the board portal meeting pack at least 7 days before the sitting.
Present and record any board direction on appetite or funding in the minutes.
Attach the minute extract to the assessment record in Archer.
checklist.done: the assessment pack is minuted at board/committee and the extract is attached in Archer.

checklist.step: Track remediation monthly against SLA
checklist.by: Vulnerability Management Lead / Security Engineering Lead
checklist.role: Vulnerability Management Lead / Security Engineering Lead
actions: Run the monthly ServiceNow report of open remediation tickets by severity and days-to-due.
Chase every ticket inside 7 days of its due date; escalate forecast misses to the IT Security Manager.
Move any breached SLA into the exception log with a recovery date.
Publish the monthly burn-down to the CISO.
checklist.done: a monthly burn-down exists and every SLA breach sits in the exception log with a recovery date.

checklist.step: Re-test closed findings before accepting closure
actions: For each ticket marked resolved, re-scan the affected asset or re-run the pentest reproduction steps.
Attach the clean re-scan evidence to the ticket before status moves to Closed.
Reopen any finding that reproduces, resetting the SLA clock from the original due date, not the reopen date.
Sample-check 10% of closures monthly for evidence quality.
checklist.done: no finding closes without attached re-test evidence, and reproducing findings are reopened on the original clock.

checklist.step: Feed assessment results into the annual BMA reporting cycle
actions: Extract the assessment date, coverage statement, top residual risks and remediation status for the annual cyber return prepared with the year-end BMA statutory filing.
Reconcile the numbers quoted in the return to the Archer registers so the filing never overstates posture.
Flag to the Head of Compliance any open critical finding that the return must disclose.
File the reconciliation with the return workpapers.
checklist.done: the annual return's cyber content reconciles line-by-line to the Archer registers.

checklist.step: Retain the full assessment evidence bundle
actions: Assemble: signed scope statement, threat catalogue version, scan exports, pentest report, scoring workbook, heat maps, remediation plan, acceptance memos and the board minute extract.
File in the compliance evidence repository under entity/cyber-risk-assessment/<year> with the 10-year retention label.
Verify retrieval by year and asset before closing the cycle.
checklist.done: the complete, retention-labelled bundle is filed and retrievable by year.

testing.step: Build the population of scoped assets and findings
actions: Independently re-run the CMDB critical-asset report as of the assessment kickoff date.
Extract the Archer assessment instance's asset list, finding register and acceptance register.
Extract the year's ServiceNow remediation tickets.
Record row counts and extraction dates as the signed population.
testing.done: independent CMDB, Archer and ServiceNow extracts are signed as the test population.

testing.step: Reconcile assessment coverage to the CMDB
actions: Match every CMDB critical asset to a row in the Archer assessment instance.
Any critical asset absent from the assessment is an automatic fail against the zero-exclusion threshold.
Check scope removals against the signed scope statement's stated reasons.
Document the reconciliation with matched, unmatched and explained counts.
testing.done: every critical asset is matched into the assessment or logged as a fail.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of critical findings and out-of-appetite risks.
Randomly select 20 further risk rows and 15 closed remediation tickets with a recorded seed.
Record seed, population sizes and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all critical items plus random rows is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the risk scoring on sampled rows
actions: For each sampled risk row, read the cited evidence (scan data, incident history, control test results) and independently score likelihood and impact on the methodology scale before viewing the recorded score.
Compare to the recorded score; a variance of more than one band either way is an exception.
A score citing no evidence reference is an exception regardless of value.
Note each re-performance in the workpaper with the evidence read.
testing.done: every sampled row has an independent score within one band or a logged exception.

testing.step: Trace findings to owned, dated remediation
actions: Match each sampled finding to its ServiceNow ticket and check owner, severity and due date follow the methodology's SLA table.
Confirm critical findings carried 30-day due dates from finding registration, not from ticket creation.
A finding with no ticket, or a ticket assigned to a queue rather than a person, is an exception.
testing.done: every sampled finding traces to a person-owned ticket with a correctly derived due date.

testing.step: Recompute remediation SLA maths and closure evidence
actions: For the sampled closed tickets, recompute days from finding registration to evidenced closure and compare to the severity SLA.
Open the attached re-test evidence and confirm it post-dates the fix and covers the affected asset.
A closure without re-test evidence, or with evidence pre-dating the fix, is an exception.
Check breached SLAs appear in the exception log with recovery dates.
testing.done: sampled closures show valid re-test evidence and SLA breaches are all logged.

testing.step: Verify out-of-appetite acceptances are signed and time-boxed
actions: For each out-of-appetite risk, locate the acceptance memo and check CRO signature, compensating controls, and an expiry within 12 months.
Confirm no acceptance was signed by the risk's own remediation owner.
An out-of-appetite risk with neither an acceptance nor an accelerated plan is a reportable finding.
testing.done: every out-of-appetite risk carries a compliant acceptance or an accelerated plan.

testing.step: Verify the assessment interval and board reporting
actions: Compute months between this assessment's completion and the prior one; over 12 months is a fail.
Confirm the assessment pack appears in the board portal meeting pack and the minutes record the presentation.
Confirm the annual BMA return's cyber content matches the Archer registers via the Compliance Manager's reconciliation.
testing.done: the 12-month interval held, board minuting exists, and return content reconciles.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a ticket per exception citing the asset, finding or risk row and the threshold breached.
Assign root cause (scope miss, unsupported score, SLA breach, unsigned acceptance) and a named owner.
Set remediation dates; scope-miss exceptions trigger an immediate delta assessment of the excluded asset.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has a ticket, root cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test

Sign as independent reviewer, having scored no risk and owned no sampled remediation.
Report to the risk committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.

checklist.step: Maintain the control catalogue mapped to the Cyber Code technical-controls section
actions: In the GRC platform maintain one control record per required control: MFA, privileged access, recertification, leaver revocation, encryption at rest, encryption in transit, endpoint protection, network segmentation, monitoring, patching.
On each record hold the Cyber Code section reference, the operating system of record, the coverage target and the named operator.
Review the catalogue semi-annually with the IT Security Manager and after any architecture change.
Version and date every catalogue change.
checklist.done: a versioned catalogue maps every required control to its code section, target, system and operator.

checklist.step: Enforce MFA on every interactive account
actions: In the IAM platform's admin console open Security ▸ Authentication Policies and confirm the global sign-on policy requires MFA for all interactive users, including contractors and remote access.
Enumerate policy exclusions; every exclusion must reference a logged GRC exception with a compensating control (e.g. service accounts restricted to non-interactive grant types).
Enroll new joiners in MFA during day-one provisioning; block first login until an authenticator is registered.
Export the policy configuration monthly and file it as the enforcement baseline.
checklist.done: the sign-on policy enforces MFA for all interactive users and every exclusion maps to a logged exception.

checklist.step: Monitor MFA coverage and chase gaps weekly
actions: Run the weekly report of active users versus MFA-enrolled users from the IAM platform.
Compute the coverage percentage and list every unenrolled interactive account with its owner and department.
Give owners 5 business days to enroll, then suspend the account and notify the line manager.
Record the weekly figure on the control KPI dashboard.
checklist.done: weekly coverage is computed, gaps are chased to enrollment or suspension, and the KPI is recorded.

checklist.step: Vault and broker every privileged credential
actions: Maintain the privileged-account inventory: domain admins, database SAs, network device credentials, cloud root/owner accounts and break-glass accounts.
In CyberArk confirm each is vaulted with automatic rotation and that interactive privileged sessions run through the PSM with session recording on.
Scan quarterly for privileged accounts outside the vault (direct AD queries, cloud IAM exports) and onboard or disable strays within 10 business days.
Test break-glass retrieval semi-annually and log the drill.
checklist.done: the privileged inventory reconciles to the vault, sessions are recorded, and strays are onboarded within 10 days.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly access recertification campaign
actions: In SailPoint launch the quarterly certification campaign on the first business day of the quarter, covering all application entitlements on scoped critical systems.
Route each user's entitlements to their line manager, and privileged entitlements additionally to the system owner.
Nag outstanding reviewers every 7 days; auto-revoke entitlements still undecided at day 30.
Export the campaign completion certificate and revocation list and file both.
checklist.done: the campaign closed within 30 days with a filed completion certificate and executed revocations.

checklist.step: Revoke leaver access within 24 hours of termination
actions: Consume the daily HR termination feed from Workday into the IAM platform's leaver workflow.
On the termination effective timestamp, auto-disable the directory account, revoke tokens and sessions, and vault-rotate any privileged credentials the leaver held.
For same-day involuntary exits, execute the manual kill-switch runbook within 1 hour of HR notification.
Log the disable timestamp against the HR effective timestamp for the day-count evidence trail.
checklist.done: every leaver's access is disabled within 24 hours of the HR effective time, with both timestamps logged.

checklist.step: Enforce the encryption standard at rest and in transit
actions: Maintain the encryption standard: AES-256 (or platform equivalent) at rest for databases, file stores and backups holding policyholder data; TLS 1.2+ for all data in transit; approved cipher suites listed.
Scan configuration baselines quarterly for unencrypted volumes, databases or legacy TLS endpoints and raise remediation tickets for each hit.
Gate new-system go-lives on an encryption checklist signed by the Security Engineer.
File quarterly scan results as control evidence.
checklist.done: quarterly scans show no unencrypted policyholder data stores or legacy TLS endpoints without tickets.

checklist.step: Manage certificates and keys to prevent silent expiry
actions: Maintain the certificate and key inventory with owner, expiry date and system mapping.
Configure expiry alerts at T-60 and T-30 days routed to the owning engineer.
Rotate encryption keys per the standard's schedule and record rotation evidence.
Review the inventory monthly for orphaned or unowned entries.
checklist.done: no certificate or key lacks an owner, an expiry alert, and a rotation record within schedule.

checklist.step: Keep endpoint protection coverage at target
actions: In the CrowdStrike console open Host setup and management ▸ Host management and reconcile the sensor count against the CMDB endpoint inventory.
List endpoints with no sensor, stale sensors (no check-in > 7 days) and prevention policies below baseline.
Raise tickets to deploy or repair within 5 business days; isolate unmanageable endpoints from the network.
Record the coverage percentage on the monthly KPI pack against the 98% target.
checklist.done: sensor coverage reconciles to the CMDB at ≥98% with tickets on every gap.

checklist.step: Operate 24/7 monitoring and alert triage
actions: Confirm the log-source inventory in Splunk covers the scoped critical systems: IAM, PAM, EDR, network, policy admin platform and cloud control planes.
Triage alerts against the severity matrix: acknowledge P1 within 15 minutes, P2 within 1 hour, per the SOC runbook.
Escalate confirmed incidents to the Incident Response Lead through the on-call rota.
Report weekly on alert volumes, triage SLA attainment and any log source silent > 24 hours.
checklist.done: all critical log sources report, triage SLAs are met, and silent sources are flagged within 24 hours.

checklist.step: Enforce patch and vulnerability SLAs
actions: Run weekly authenticated scans and assign findings to owners with SLA due dates: critical 14 days, high 30 days, medium 90 days.
Track the ageing report daily and chase items inside 7 days of due.
Escalate breached SLAs to the IT Security Manager and log them in the exception register with recovery dates.
Publish the monthly patch-compliance percentage per platform.
checklist.done: findings carry owned SLA dates, breaches are escalated and logged, and monthly compliance is published.

checklist.step: Review network segmentation and firewall baselines
actions: Review firewall rulebases semi-annually against the documented segmentation model separating user, server, policy-admin and DMZ zones.
Remove or justify every any-any rule and every rule without a named owner and business reason.
Verify the policy admin platform and databases accept connections only from approved application tiers.
File the signed rulebase review with the control evidence.
checklist.done: the semi-annual rulebase review is signed with no unjustified any-any or ownerless rules.

checklist.step: Log control exceptions with compensating controls
actions: Record every deviation (MFA exclusion, unvaulted account, SLA breach, unencrypted legacy store) as a GRC exception with business reason, compensating control and expiry ≤ 12 months.
Reject exception requests without a compensating control.
Run the monthly expiring-exception report and force closure or renewal with fresh risk assessment.
Feed the open-exception count into the monthly KPI pack.
checklist.done: every deviation is a dated, compensated exception and expiries are actioned monthly.

checklist.step: Publish the monthly control KPI pack to the CISO
actions: Compile: MFA coverage, PAM vault reconciliation, recertification status, leaver revocation timeliness, EDR coverage, patch compliance, SIEM source health and open exceptions.
Mark each KPI green/amber/red against the standard's targets and trend it over 12 months.
Review with the Chief Info Security Officer and record agreed actions on red KPIs.
File each month's pack in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the monthly pack is reviewed with the CISO, red KPIs carry actions, and packs are filed.

checklist.step: Retain operating evidence per the retention requirement
actions: File monthly configuration baselines, campaign exports, revocation logs, scan results and KPI packs in the compliance evidence repository under entity/technical-controls/<year-month>.
Apply the 10-year retention label.
Spot-check quarterly that a named month's evidence is retrievable end-to-end.
checklist.done: monthly evidence is filed, retention-labelled and passes the quarterly retrieval spot-check.

testing.step: Build the quarter's population of accounts, leavers, endpoints and campaigns
actions: Extract the active-account list from the IAM platform as at quarter end, split interactive versus service accounts.
Obtain the quarter's termination list directly from HR in Workday, not from the IAM feed being tested.
Extract the endpoint inventory from the CMDB and the sensor list from CrowdStrike.
Extract the quarter's SailPoint campaign records and Qualys finding tickets, and sign the population with row counts.
testing.done: independent extracts from IAM, HR, CMDB, EDR, IGA and the scanner are signed as the population.

testing.step: Reconcile the account list to HR headcount
actions: Match every interactive account to an active employee or contractor in the HR extract.
List accounts with no HR match (orphans) and HR actives with no account as reconciliation exceptions.
Confirm each orphan is a documented service or shared account with a logged exception, otherwise fail it.
testing.done: every interactive account maps to an HR active or a logged exception; orphans are failed.

testing.step: Recompute MFA coverage and inspect exclusions
actions: From the IAM extract, independently compute MFA enrollment over interactive accounts and compare to the reported KPI.
Open the sign-on policy in the console and list every exclusion group and its members.
Trace each excluded member to a GRC exception with compensating control; an untraced exclusion is a fail against the 100% threshold.
Screenshot the policy configuration into the workpaper.
testing.done: recomputed coverage matches the KPI and every exclusion traces to a logged exception.

testing.step: Sample privileged accounts and verify vaulting and session recording
actions: Select 15 privileged accounts across domain, database, network and cloud tiers with a recorded seed.
In CyberArk verify each is vaulted with rotation within policy and locate a session recording from the quarter for accounts used interactively.
Query AD and cloud IAM directly for privileged group members not present in the vault inventory.
Any unvaulted privileged account found is an exception with immediate escalation to the CISO.
testing.done: sampled accounts are vaulted with recordings, and direct queries surface no unvaulted stragglers.

testing.step: Re-perform a slice of the quarterly recertification
actions: Verify the campaign launched on schedule and closed within 30 days with a completion certificate.
Sample 20 certified entitlements and confirm the recorded reviewer was the line manager or system owner, not the user themselves.
For 5 sampled revocation decisions, verify the entitlement is actually gone from the target system, not just marked revoked.
An entitlement still live after a revocation decision is an exception.
testing.done: the campaign closed on time and sampled revocations are proven executed in the target systems.

testing.step: Recompute leaver revocation day counts
actions: For every leaver in the HR extract (100%, no sampling), compare the HR termination effective timestamp to the IAM disable timestamp.
Compute the elapsed hours; anything over 24 hours is a fail against the threshold.
For 10 sampled leavers, additionally query last-login timestamps to prove no post-termination access occurred.
Post-termination activity on a live account is a reportable incident, not a test exception.
testing.done: every leaver shows ≤24-hour revocation and sampled last-logins show no post-termination access.

testing.step: Verify encryption and endpoint coverage on a sample
actions: Reconcile the CrowdStrike sensor list to the CMDB endpoint inventory and recompute coverage against the 98% target.
Sample 10 policyholder-data stores from the data inventory and inspect their at-rest encryption configuration with the Security Engineer.
Sample 5 external endpoints and verify TLS configuration meets the standard using the quarterly scan output.
Uncovered endpoints or unencrypted stores without logged exceptions are fails.
testing.done: coverage recomputes at ≥98% and sampled stores and endpoints meet the encryption standard.

testing.step: Test monitoring health and patch SLA maths
actions: In Splunk compare the log-source inventory to actual events received in the quarter; list sources silent > 24 hours and check each was flagged at the time.
Sample 10 P1/P2 alerts and recompute acknowledgment times against the 15-minute/1-hour SLAs.
Sample 15 critical/high findings from Qualys and recompute days from detection to remediation against the 14/30-day SLAs.
Unflagged silent sources and unlogged SLA breaches are exceptions.
testing.done: source health, triage times and patch day counts recompute within SLA or sit in the exception log.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a ticket per exception citing the account, endpoint, entitlement or finding and the threshold breached.
Assign root cause (feed gap, policy exclusion drift, reviewer neglect, resourcing) and a named owner.
Set remediation dates; post-termination-access findings open an incident and a self-report assessment with the Head of Compliance.
Carry open exceptions into next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has a ticket, root cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute exception rates against the MFA, leaver, recertification and EDR thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references.
Sign as independent reviewer, having administered no tested control and approved no sampled exception.
Report to the risk committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with conclusion, exception rates and committee reporting date is filed.

checklist.step: Maintain the incident response plan with all five phases defined
actions: Keep the IR plan current across detection, containment, eradication, recovery and communication, with named role assignments for each phase.
Maintain per-scenario playbooks for ransomware, data exfiltration, business email compromise, vendor compromise and DDoS.
Review the plan annually and within 30 days of any severity-1 incident closure.
Version the plan in the document management repository with an approval page signed by the Chief Info Security Officer.
checklist.done: a current, CISO-signed plan with five phases and scenario playbooks sits in the document repository.

checklist.step: Define the materiality criteria that start the BMA notification clock
actions: Document the tests making a cyber incident material to the BMA: disruption of a critical service, policyholder data compromise, financial loss above the stated threshold, or third-party compromise affecting the insurer's operations.
State explicitly that the 72-hour clock runs from the materiality determination timestamp, and the 14-day follow-up clock from the initial notification.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the criteria against the Cyber Code's notification wording.
Publish the criteria inside the IR plan and the compliance manual.
checklist.done: counsel-confirmed materiality criteria with both clock definitions are published in the plan.

checklist.step: Maintain the 24/7 escalation roster and contact tree
actions: Keep the on-call rota covering SOC, Incident Response Lead, CISO, Head of Compliance, Regulatory Counsel and communications, with primary and deputy per seat.
Verify every contact monthly with a test page; replace stale entries within 2 business days.
Store the tree in the SOAR platform and a printed out-of-band copy in case corporate systems are down.
Log each monthly verification.
checklist.done: the roster is verified monthly with deputies per seat and an out-of-band copy exists.

checklist.step: Wire detection-to-IR handoff in the SOAR platform
actions: Configure SOAR playbooks so a confirmed P1/P2 detection auto-opens an incident case, pages the on-call responder and starts the case timeline.
Embed the materiality-assessment task into the case template so it cannot be skipped, with the 24/48/68-hour timer alerts to the Head of Compliance.
Test the automation quarterly with a synthetic alert and record the run.
Fix any failed handoff within 5 business days.
checklist.done: P1/P2 detections auto-open timed cases with an unskippable materiality task, and quarterly synthetics pass.

checklist.step: Plan and run the annual IR exercise
actions: Choose a scenario the insurer has not exercised in the last two cycles (e.g. ransomware on the policy admin platform with data exfiltration).
Schedule the exercise within 12 months of the prior one and invite every roster seat, including Regulatory Counsel and communications.
Run the tabletop through all five phases, injecting complications (backup failure, media enquiry, vendor outage).
Record attendance, decisions and timings in the exercise report.
checklist.done: the exercise ran within 12 months with full roster attendance and a timed, documented scenario.

checklist.step: Exercise the 72-hour notification workflow end to end
actions: Inside the exercise, run the materiality determination on the scenario facts and timestamp it.
Draft a mock BMA initial notification using the counsel-approved template: incident summary, services affected, containment status, next update commitment.
Walk the draft through counsel clearance and simulate submission, measuring elapsed time against the 72-hour clock.
Log the measured duration and any bottleneck in the exercise report.
checklist.done: the exercise proves the notification path completes inside 72 hours, with bottlenecks logged.

checklist.step: Include forensic readiness in the exercise and the plan
actions: Verify the forensic toolkit (imaging, memory capture, log preservation) is licensed, current and accessible out-of-band.
In the exercise, walk the evidence-preservation steps: isolate, image, hash, chain-of-custody form.
Confirm log retention on critical systems meets the plan's minimum look-back (12 months hot, 24 months archived).
Report gaps to the Incident Response Lead for the remediation list.
checklist.done: the toolkit is verified, preservation steps are walked, and retention look-backs are confirmed.

checklist.step: Convert exercise lessons learned into plan changes
actions: Within 15 business days of the exercise, hold the debrief and log every finding as a ticket with owner and due date.
Redline the IR plan for accepted changes and re-issue the version with the CISO's signature.
Track findings to closure; overdue findings escalate to the CISO monthly.
Attach the finding log to the exercise report.
checklist.done: every exercise finding is a tracked ticket and accepted changes are re-issued in a signed plan version.

checklist.step: On a live incident, run the materiality determination with a timestamp
actions: Convene the CISO, Incident Response Lead and Head of Compliance as soon as scoping facts allow — do not wait for full eradication.
Apply the materiality criteria to the known facts and record the determination, the facts relied on, and the exact timestamp in the SOAR case.
If facts are insufficient, record the interim not-yet-determinable status and re-assess at least every 24 hours.
A material determination immediately starts the 72-hour timer visible on the case.
checklist.done: the case holds a timestamped determination (or a re-assessed interim status) with the facts relied on.

checklist.step: Submit the BMA initial notification within 72 hours
actions: Draft the initial notification from the case facts: incident nature, systems and services affected, policyholder impact known so far, containment actions and the committed follow-up date.
Obtain Regulatory Counsel clearance — target clearance inside 48 hours to protect the 72-hour clock.
Submit to the entity's BMA supervisory contact through the established channel and request written acknowledgment.
Log the submission timestamp in the SOAR case and file the notification and acknowledgment in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the cleared notification is with the BMA inside 72 hours with the timestamp and acknowledgment logged.

checklist.step: File the follow-up report within 14 days of the initial notification
actions: Start the 14-day countdown at the initial notification's submission timestamp.
Compile the follow-up: root cause, full impact assessment, remediation actions with dates, and control changes, drawing on the forensic report.
Clear through Regulatory Counsel and submit by day 14; if facts remain open, submit the interim position by day 14 and commit a further update date.
Log submission and file the report with the case.
checklist.done: the follow-up (or interim position) reached the BMA within 14 days of the initial notification.

checklist.step: Fork PIPA breach assessment for personal-information incidents
actions: For any incident touching personal information, open the PIPA breach assessment in parallel with the BMA workstream.
Assess likely adverse effect on individuals per PIPA and determine whether notification to the Privacy Commissioner and affected individuals is required.
Coordinate timing with the Head of Compliance so BMA and PrivCom communications tell one consistent story.
Record the assessment outcome in the incident case.
checklist.done: every personal-information incident carries a documented PIPA assessment coordinated with the BMA track.

checklist.step: Track incident root-cause remediation to closure
actions: Load every remediation action from the post-incident review into the GRC action tracker with owner and date.
Review monthly; forecast misses on actions cited in a BMA follow-up report trigger a written update to the Head of Compliance for onward notification.
Collect closure evidence before marking complete.
Report open incident actions to the risk committee quarterly.
checklist.done: every post-incident action is tracked to evidenced closure or a notified date change.

checklist.step: Report incidents and exercise results to the board
actions: Include in the board cyber report: incident counts by severity, material incidents with notification timelines, exercise results and open remediation.
Upload to the board portal pack and present at the next scheduled sitting; severity-1 incidents are reported out-of-cycle within 5 business days.
Record board direction in the minutes and attach the extract to the case records.
checklist.done: incidents and exercise results are minuted at board with severity-1 items reported out-of-cycle.

checklist.step: Retain incident and exercise records
actions: File per incident: the SOAR case export, materiality determination, notifications, acknowledgments, forensic report and post-incident review.
File per exercise: scenario, attendance, timings, findings and the re-issued plan version.
Apply the 10-year retention label and verify retrieval by incident id and year.
checklist.done: every incident and exercise bundle is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by id.

testing.step: Build the period's incident and exercise population
actions: Extract all security incident tickets from ServiceNow and all SOAR cases for the period.
Extract the notification log and exercise records from the GRC platform.
Record row counts and extraction dates as the signed population.
testing.done: signed extracts of incidents, cases, notifications and exercises exist with counts.

testing.step: Reconcile SIEM cases to ServiceNow tickets
actions: Match every P1/P2 SIEM case to a ServiceNow incident ticket and vice versa.
List cases with no ticket (untracked incidents) and tickets with no case (unmonitored sources) as completeness exceptions.
Resolve or log every mismatch before sampling.
testing.done: the two systems reconcile or every mismatch is a logged completeness exception.

testing.step: Verify every incident carries a materiality determination
actions: Take 100% of P1/P2 incidents and a random sample of 15 lower-severity incidents.
Confirm each carries a timestamped determination naming the criteria applied and the facts relied on.
For interim not-yet-determinable statuses, check re-assessment happened at least every 24 hours.
Independently re-apply the criteria to 10 not-material conclusions; one you would overturn is an exception.
testing.done: all sampled incidents carry defensible, timestamped determinations with compliant re-assessment cadence.

testing.step: Recompute the 72-hour clock on every material incident
actions: For each material incident, compute elapsed hours from the determination timestamp to the BMA submission timestamp.
Anything over 72 hours is a fail; verify the submission evidence is the actual sent notification, not a draft.
Confirm a BMA acknowledgment is on file for each notification.
Capture both timestamps into the workpaper.
testing.done: every material incident shows ≤72 elapsed hours with sent evidence and acknowledgment on file.

testing.step: Recompute the 14-day follow-up deadline
actions: For each initial notification, compute days to the follow-up report's submission timestamp.
Anything over 14 days is a fail; an interim position filed by day 14 with a committed update date passes.
Verify the follow-up content covers root cause, impact and dated remediation.
Check counsel clearance records exist for each submission.
testing.done: every follow-up landed within 14 days (or a compliant interim) with counsel clearance evidenced.

testing.step: Verify the annual exercise ran and covered the plan
actions: Compute months since the prior exercise; over 12 is a fail.
Read the exercise report and confirm all five phases were walked, the notification workflow was timed, and every roster seat attended or sent a deputy.
Confirm the timed notification path completed inside 72 hours in the exercise.
testing.done: a within-12-months exercise covering all phases and the timed notification path is evidenced.

testing.step: Trace lessons learned to closed plan changes
actions: Match every exercise and post-incident finding to a ticket with owner and due date.
Sample 10 closed findings and verify the closure evidence (plan redline, config change, retraining record) actually exists.
Findings open past due without escalation are exceptions.
testing.done: findings trace to owned tickets and sampled closures carry real evidence.

testing.step: Verify PIPA assessments on personal-information incidents
actions: Identify every incident in the population flagged as touching personal information.
Confirm each carries a PIPA breach assessment with an adverse-effect conclusion and a notify/do-not-notify decision.
Re-read 5 assessments and confirm the conclusions are supportable on the recorded facts.
A personal-information incident with no assessment is a reportable finding.
testing.done: every personal-information incident carries a supportable, documented PIPA assessment.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a ticket per exception citing the incident id, the clock or control that failed, and the impact.
Assign root cause (late determination, clearance bottleneck, roster gap, untracked case) and a named owner.

checklist.step: Confirm the filing obligation and due date for each Bermuda entity
actions: List every group entity registered with the BMA from the legal entity register, with registration class and financial year end.
Read the current BMA filing instructions for the annual statutory return and confirm the cyber certification/return component and its format for each class.
Enter each entity's filing deadline into the regulatory calendar with T-90/T-60/T-30 tasks.
Record the instruction version relied on with a dated capture.
checklist.done: every Bermuda entity has a calendared deadline tied to a dated capture of the current BMA instructions.

checklist.step: Maintain the three-lines-of-defence roles matrix for cyber
actions: Maintain the matrix naming first-line control operators (IT Security Manager and platform teams), second-line oversight (Operational Risk Manager, Chief Risk Officer) and third-line assurance (Chief Audit Executive) for every cyber control family.
Verify no person occupies two lines for the same control family — self-review voids the model.
Refresh the matrix on every relevant staffing change and at least quarterly.
Store the current matrix in the GRC platform linked to the certification record.
checklist.done: a current matrix names all three lines per control family with no self-review conflicts.

checklist.step: Collect first-line control attestations
actions: Issue attestation requests to each first-line control operator listed in the matrix, 60 days before the filing deadline.
Each attestation states the control operated as designed for the year, citing the KPI packs and test results that prove it, or discloses the exceptions.
Reject attestations that cite no evidence — a bare signature is not an attestation.
Compile the signed set for the certification file.
checklist.done: a signed, evidence-cited attestation exists for every first-line control family, exceptions disclosed.

checklist.step: Obtain the second-line risk opinion
actions: Draft the second-line opinion on the cyber control environment from the year's risk assessment, exception register and incident record.
State explicitly whether residual risk sat within appetite for the year and list out-of-appetite periods with their acceptances.
Have the Chief Risk Officer countersign the opinion.
Deliver to the certification file 45 days before the deadline.
checklist.done: a CRO-countersigned second-line opinion with an explicit appetite statement is on file 45 days out.

checklist.step: Obtain the third-line audit coverage confirmation
actions: Summarise the internal audit work performed on cyber controls in the period: audits completed, ratings issued, open findings and overdue actions.
Confirm in writing that independent assurance coverage existed over the control families the certification will attest to.
Flag any control family with no third-line coverage in the last 24 months so the certification can disclose it.
Deliver the confirmation to the certification file 45 days before the deadline.
checklist.done: a written third-line coverage confirmation, with uncovered families flagged, is on file 45 days out.

checklist.step: Draft the certification and reconcile every answer to evidence
actions: Complete the BMA return/certification questions from the attestation set, risk opinion, audit confirmation and the Archer registers.
Build the evidence index: every answer cross-referenced to the specific document, register extract or KPI supporting it.
Where the honest answer is qualified (control gap, open critical finding), draft the qualification with its remediation plan rather than rounding up to compliant.
Route the draft and index to the Security GRC Analyst for an independent tie-out.
checklist.done: a fully drafted certification with a complete answer-to-evidence index and honest qualifications exists.

checklist.step: Tie out the draft against source registers
actions: Re-open each cited register (risk assessment, exception log, incident log) and verify the certification's figures and statements match the source as at the reporting date.
Mark each answer tied-out or discrepant; discrepancies go back to the Compliance Manager for correction, never silent adjustment.
Sign the tie-out sheet and attach it to the certification file.
checklist.done: every answer is marked tied-out on a signed sheet, with discrepancies corrected at source.

checklist.step: CISO review and signature
actions: Read the full certification, the qualifications and the evidence index.
Challenge any answer that reads better than the KPI packs and incident record the CISO has seen through the year.
Sign the certification as the accountable executive, dating the signature.
Return the signed copy to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: the CISO has signed a certification consistent with the year's known posture, qualifications included.

checklist.step: Obtain board or committee ratification
actions: Place the signed certification and its qualification summary on the board (or delegated committee) agenda ahead of the filing deadline.
Upload the pack to the board portal at least 7 days before the sitting.
Record the ratification resolution in the minutes and provide the extract for the certification file.
Diarise the next year's ratification slot immediately.
checklist.done: a minuted ratification resolution pre-dating the filing is in the certification file.

checklist.step: File the certification with the annual statutory return
actions: Submit the certification/return through the BMA's electronic filing channel with the entity's annual statutory filing package, per the current filing instructions.
Verify the upload rendered correctly — re-open the submitted document from the portal, not the local copy.
Capture the submission confirmation with its timestamp.
Notify the Head of Compliance and CISO of the completed filing the same day.
checklist.done: the certification is submitted with the statutory package and the timestamped confirmation is captured.

checklist.step: File the acknowledgment and archive the submission record
actions: Save the BMA acknowledgment or portal confirmation into the compliance evidence repository beside the filed certification.
Archive the complete bundle: certification, attestations, opinions, tie-out sheet, evidence index, board extract, submission confirmation.
Apply the 10-year retention label and verify retrieval by entity and filing year.
checklist.done: the full filing bundle with acknowledgment is archived, labelled and retrievable.

checklist.step: Answer BMA follow-up queries within 14 days
actions: Log every BMA query on the filing in the regulatory system the day it arrives, starting the 14-day response countdown.
Assemble the response with the Compliance Manager, citing the evidence index rather than producing new claims.
Clear responses touching qualified answers through the Head of Compliance before sending.
Send within 14 days of receipt and log the response date; request an extension in writing before day 14 if genuinely needed.
checklist.done: every query shows a logged receipt date and a response (or written extension request) within 14 days.

checklist.step: Manage qualified answers to remediation
actions: Load the remediation plan behind each qualified answer into the GRC action tracker with owner and date.
Review monthly; a slipping action that was represented to the BMA triggers a proactive written update to the Authority.
Sign closure only on evidence, and mark the item resolved for next year's certification.
Correct a filed certification within 14 days of discovering any material inaccuracy.
checklist.done: every qualification is tracked to evidenced closure and inaccuracies are corrected within 14 days.

checklist.step: Arm the next filing cycle
actions: Roll the regulatory calendar entry to the next financial year end with T-90/T-60/T-30 tasks to named current staff.
Diarise the attestation-request launch at T-60 and the tie-out at T-30.
Note format changes the BMA announced during the year against the calendar entry.
Confirm reminder recipients after any staffing change.
checklist.done: next cycle's calendar entry, task chain and named recipients are in place.

checklist.step: Log filing exceptions with disposition
actions: Log any late filing, late query response or post-filing correction as a GRC exception with root cause.
Assess each against the self-report materiality criteria with the Head of Compliance.
Track the exception's remediation to closure and cite it in next year's procedure review.
checklist.done: every filing defect is a logged, assessed exception tracked to closure.

testing.step: Build the population of certifications due and filed
actions: Independently list every BMA-registered group entity from the legal entity register and corporate secretarial records.
For each, determine the statutory filing deadline from the BMA instructions in force for that year end.
Extract the filed certifications and submission confirmations from the compliance evidence repository.
Sign the population with entity counts and deadlines.
testing.done: a signed entity-by-entity population with independent deadlines and filed records exists.

testing.step: Reconcile entities due against certifications filed
actions: Match every due entity to a filed certification; a due entity with no filing is an automatic fail.
Compare each submission timestamp to the statutory deadline and list late filings.
Verify each filing's confirmation is a portal-issued record, not an internal note.
testing.done: every due entity traces to an on-time, portal-confirmed filing or a logged fail.

testing.step: Sample certification answers and re-perform them to evidence
actions: Select 15 answers per filed certification with a recorded seed, weighted toward unqualified 'compliant' answers.
For each, open the evidence-index reference and independently judge whether the cited evidence supports the answer as at the reporting date.
An answer whose evidence shows an open gap the certification did not qualify is an exception of the most serious class.
Record each re-performance with the evidence read.
testing.done: sampled answers are independently supported by their cited evidence or logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Verify signatory authority and board ratification
actions: Confirm the CISO signature is present and dated before submission.
Locate the ratification resolution in the board portal minutes and check its date pre-dates the filing.
Verify the pack presented to the board included the qualification summary, not a cleaned version.
testing.done: a dated CISO signature and pre-filing board ratification over the full qualification set are evidenced.

testing.step: Test the three-lines matrix for completeness and segregation
actions: Check every cyber control family in the matrix has a named person in all three lines for the whole period.
Cross-check names against HR records for the period to catch vacancies papered over with former staff.
Verify no individual appears in two lines for the same family; any self-review voids that attestation chain and is an exception.
testing.done: the matrix shows continuous, segregated coverage across all three lines for every family.

testing.step: Verify the attestation chain behind the certification
actions: Confirm a signed first-line attestation exists per control family and cites real evidence.
Confirm the second-line opinion carries the CRO countersignature and an explicit appetite statement.
Confirm the third-line coverage confirmation exists and its flagged uncovered families appear as disclosures in the certification.
A certification answer resting on a missing or evidence-free attestation is an exception.
testing.done: every certification answer rests on a complete, signed, evidence-cited attestation chain.

testing.step: Recompute BMA query response clocks
actions: Extract the BMA query log for the filing and compute days from logged receipt to sent response for each query.
Anything over 14 days without a pre-day-14 written extension request is a fail.
Sample 3 responses and verify the sent content matches the cleared version.
testing.done: every query shows a ≤14-day response or a timely extension, with sent content matching clearance.

testing.step: Trace qualifications to live remediation
actions: For each qualified answer, locate the GRC action with owner and date.
Verify monthly review evidence and that any slip against a BMA-represented date produced a proactive update to the Authority.
Confirm closures carry evidence, and corrections to the filed certification went in within 14 days of discovery.
testing.done: every qualification traces to tracked remediation with BMA updates on slips and timely corrections.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a ticket per exception citing the entity, answer or query and the threshold breached.
Assign root cause (missed entity, overstated answer, vacant seat, clock breach) and a named owner.
Overstated-answer exceptions open a correction assessment with Regulatory Counsel immediately.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has a ticket, root cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-missed-filing and evidence-support thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references.
Sign as independent reviewer, excluding from the sample any answer resting on the third line's own audit work; those answers are reviewed by the Chief Risk Officer instead.
Report to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with conclusion, segregation note and committee reporting date is filed.
