checklist.step: Maintain the vendor inventory with criticality tiering
actions: Keep every active supplier in the Coupa/Ariba vendor master with service description, data access level, and criticality tier (critical / material / standard).
Reconcile the vendor master to the AP spend file quarterly to surface engaged-but-unregistered suppliers.
Tag vendors supporting critical services or holding policyholder data for the enhanced oversight track.
Publish the tiered inventory to the Third-Party Risk Manager monthly.
checklist.done: the vendor master reconciles to AP spend quarterly and every vendor carries a current tier.

checklist.step: Classify arrangements against the BMA materiality tests
actions: Apply the BMA Operational Resilience and Outsourcing Guidance Notes (2025) materiality tests to each arrangement: criticality to insurance operations, policyholder impact on failure, data sensitivity, substitutability.
Record the classification with the tests applied and the conclusion in Archer, dated and signed.
Re-classify on any material scope change to the service.
Route every 'material' conclusion to the Chief Risk Officer for confirmation.
checklist.done: every arrangement carries a dated, test-based classification with CRO confirmation on material calls.

checklist.step: Complete pre-contract due diligence before signature
actions: Open the due diligence record in Archer at sourcing start: security posture, financial soundness, operational capability, sub-outsourcing chain, jurisdiction exposure.
Require completion and a documented risk conclusion before the contract can route for signature — Icertis blocks signature workflow without the Archer clearance reference.
Scale the pack by tier: full assessment for material vendors, lightweight questionnaire for standard.
File the completed pack against the vendor record.
checklist.done: no contract reaches signature without a completed, tier-appropriate due diligence pack and clearance reference.

checklist.step: Assess vendor security posture from independent assurance
actions: Collect the vendor's current SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificate plus bridge letter, and read the exceptions and complementary user-entity controls.
Map each report exception to the insurer's exposure and require a vendor remediation statement for relevant ones.
For vendors holding policyholder data with no independent report, run the security questionnaire and require evidence, not assertions.
Record the security conclusion on the due diligence record.
checklist.done: every material vendor's security conclusion rests on a current independent report or evidenced questionnaire.

checklist.step: Check financial soundness and ownership
actions: Obtain the vendor's latest audited financial statements or a credit report and score solvency, profitability and dependency on a single client.
Screen ownership and sanctions exposure through the compliance screening process before onboarding.
Flag vendors with going-concern doubts or opaque ownership to the Third-Party Risk Manager for a risk decision.
Record the financial conclusion on the due diligence record.
checklist.done: every material vendor carries a documented financial and ownership conclusion pre-signature.

checklist.step: Assess concentration risk across the vendor book
actions: Map critical services to their providers and identify single points of failure: one vendor supporting multiple critical services, or multiple critical services on one cloud region.
Quantify the operational impact of each concentration's simultaneous failure using the business-impact analysis.
Report concentrations above tolerance to the risk committee with mitigation options (second source, enhanced exit plan, contractual resilience commitments).
Refresh the concentration map semi-annually.
checklist.done: a semi-annually refreshed concentration map exists with above-tolerance items reported and mitigated.

checklist.step: Enforce the mandatory contract clauses
actions: Apply the outsourcing clause template in Icertis: audit and access rights for the insurer and the BMA, security and data-protection obligations, incident notification within 24 hours, sub-outsourcing consent, termination assistance and exit obligations.
Run the clause-compliance check on every material contract before signature; deviations need Regulatory Counsel approval logged in the contract record.
Re-paper legacy material contracts missing mandatory clauses at renewal, tracked to a dated plan.
Store executed contracts in Icertis with clause metadata tagged.
checklist.done: every material contract carries the mandatory clauses or a counsel-approved, logged deviation.

checklist.step: Notify the BMA of material outsourcing before commencement
actions: For each arrangement classified material, prepare the BMA notification per the guidance notes: service description, provider details, materiality rationale, risk assessment summary and exit arrangements.
Submit to the entity's supervisory contact before the arrangement commences, and diarise any BMA response window before go-live.
File the notification and any BMA response with the vendor record and the compliance evidence repository.
Notify the BMA of material changes to an existing notified arrangement on the same basis.
checklist.done: every material arrangement shows a pre-commencement BMA notification with responses filed.

checklist.step: Onboard the vendor into monitoring
actions: Create the vendor's monitoring record: SLA definitions from the contract, incident-notification contacts, review tier and next review date.
Wire vendor incident reports into ServiceNow so provider outages open tickets against the vendor record.
Set the Archer annual-review task at T-60 days before the review anniversary.
Confirm the vendor's incident contact answers a test notification within the contractual window.
checklist.done: the vendor is live in monitoring with SLAs, incident routing, a scheduled review and a tested contact.

checklist.step: Run the annual review per vendor tier
actions: For material vendors, complete the annual review within 12 months of the prior one: SLA attainment, incident history, refreshed SOC 2/ISO evidence, financial re-check, sub-outsourcing changes.
For critical vendors, add a service-resilience discussion with the provider and validate their BCP test results.
Score the vendor red/amber/green and record findings with owners and dates in Archer.
Standard-tier vendors get a lightweight desktop review every 24 months.
checklist.done: every material vendor shows a within-12-months review with a recorded score and owned findings.

checklist.step: Monitor SLAs and vendor incidents continuously
actions: Track monthly SLA reports from material vendors against contractual targets; chase missing reports within 5 business days.
Log every vendor incident affecting the insurer, and verify the vendor's notification arrived within the contractual 24-hour window.
Escalate repeated SLA misses or late notifications to the Vendor Manager for the review record.
Feed vendor incidents touching security or data to the Incident Response Lead the same day.
checklist.done: SLA attainment and incident notifications are tracked monthly with breaches escalated and security events forwarded.

checklist.step: Test exit plans for critical vendors
actions: Maintain a documented exit plan per critical vendor: data return and destruction, service transition options, in-house fallback, timeline and cost estimate.
Test each plan at least every 24 months — desktop walkthrough minimum, data-extraction rehearsal for vendors holding policyholder data.
Log test results and gaps as findings with owners in Archer.
Update the plan after any material service change.
checklist.done: every critical vendor has an exit plan tested within 24 months with findings tracked.

checklist.step: Track vendor findings and remediation
actions: Track every due diligence, review and exit-test finding in Archer with owner, severity and due date.
Chase vendor-side remediations through the Vendor Coordinator with written vendor commitments.
Escalate overdue material-vendor findings to the Chief Risk Officer monthly.
Close findings only on evidence.
checklist.done: all vendor findings are tracked with written commitments and evidenced closure.

checklist.step: Escalate deteriorating vendors to the risk committee
actions: Review red-scored vendors, repeated SLA breaches and financial red flags at the risk committee quarterly.
Decide and minute the action per vendor: remediation with milestones, contract restriction, exit-plan activation, or documented risk acceptance capped at 12 months.
Notify the BMA where a material provider's deterioration threatens a critical service, coordinated through the Head of Compliance.
Record decisions against the vendor record in Archer.
checklist.done: deteriorating vendors carry minuted committee decisions and BMA notification where required.

checklist.step: Retain the oversight evidence trail
actions: File per vendor: due diligence pack, classification, contract clause check, BMA notification, review reports, SLA history, exit-test records.
Apply the retention label of 10 years past contract termination.
Verify retrieval by vendor name and year during the annual programme review.
checklist.done: every vendor's oversight trail is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable.

testing.step: Build the vendor and contract population

Extract the 12-month AP spend file from the ERP as an independent completeness source.
Extract the Archer classification, review and finding registers.
Sign the population with row counts and extraction dates.
testing.done: signed extracts from procurement, CLM, AP and Archer form the test population.

testing.step: Reconcile vendor master to AP spend to catch shadow vendors
actions: Match every AP payee above the de-minimis threshold to a vendor-master record with a criticality tier.
List payees with no vendor record or no classification as completeness exceptions.
For each shadow vendor found, determine whether the service would classify as material — an unclassified material service is a fail.
testing.done: all significant payees trace to classified vendor records or logged exceptions.

testing.step: Sample material contracts and verify due diligence pre-dated signature
actions: Take 100% of material contracts signed in the period and 10 random standard-tier contracts with a recorded seed.
Compare the Archer due diligence completion date to the Icertis signature date; diligence closing after signature is a fail.
Check the pack's contents match the tier requirement (security, financial, sub-outsourcing, jurisdiction).
Verify the signature workflow carried the Archer clearance reference.
testing.done: every sampled contract shows tier-complete due diligence closed before signature.

testing.step: Re-perform the materiality classification on a sample
actions: Select 10 arrangements spanning the tiers, including at least 3 classified non-material.
Independently apply the BMA guidance tests to the service facts before reading the recorded conclusion.
A non-material classification you would overturn is an exception of the most serious class, since it bypasses notification and enhanced oversight.
Record the re-performance rationale per arrangement.
testing.done: sampled classifications withstand independent re-application of the BMA tests or are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Verify BMA notifications for material arrangements
actions: For every arrangement classified material, locate the BMA notification and confirm its date precedes service commencement.
Check the notification content covers provider, service, materiality rationale and exit arrangements per the guidance notes.
Confirm material changes to notified arrangements were re-notified.
A commenced material arrangement with no notification is a reportable finding requiring a self-report assessment.
testing.done: every material arrangement traces to a compliant, pre-commencement notification.

testing.step: Test review currency and content across the material book
actions: For 100% of material vendors, compute months since the last completed review; over 12 is a fail.
Sample 10 reviews and verify they contain refreshed independent assurance, SLA history, financial re-check and scored findings.
Confirm Coupa actually blocks purchase orders for the lapsed-review vendors found, if any.
testing.done: no material vendor's review exceeds 12 months, and sampled reviews are substantively complete.

testing.step: Verify contract clauses in sampled material contracts
actions: Open 10 sampled material contracts in Icertis and verify the mandatory clauses: BMA and insurer audit rights, 24-hour incident notification, sub-outsourcing consent, termination assistance.
Trace any missing clause to a counsel-approved deviation record or the dated re-papering plan.
A material contract missing clauses with neither is an exception.
testing.done: sampled contracts carry the mandatory clauses or documented, approved deviations.

testing.step: Verify exit-plan testing for critical vendors
actions: For 100% of critical vendors, locate the exit plan and compute months since its last test; over 24 is a fail.
Read 5 test records and confirm they exercised data return and transition steps, not just a document review sign-off.
Trace test findings to owned remediation in Archer.
testing.done: every critical vendor shows a within-24-months, substantive exit test with tracked findings.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a ticket per exception citing the vendor, contract or arrangement and the threshold breached.
Assign root cause (shadow engagement, post-signature diligence, missed notification, lapsed review) and a named owner.
Missed-notification exceptions open a self-report assessment with the Head of Compliance immediately.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has a ticket, root cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute exception rates against the due diligence, notification, review-currency and exit-test thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references.
Sign as independent reviewer, having performed no sampled diligence and owned no sampled relationship.
Report to the risk committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with conclusion, exception rates and committee reporting date is filed.

Compliance procedure documented.value: Privacy Notice Management Procedure — trigger-point inventory, PIPA s.9 content checklist (purposes, types of information, recipients, privacy officer contact, individual rights), version control, per-channel delivery mechanics and re-notice rules

Compliance procedure approved.value: Procedure and each notice version approved by Privacy Counsel and the Privacy Officer; re-approved on any change of processing purposes or PIPA guidance from the Privacy Commissioner

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven: the notice must be provided before or at the point of collection at every trigger; re-notice issues before any new use of previously collected information takes effect

Deadline reminders configured.value: The data-use register change workflow blocks a new processing purpose going live until the re-notice task is closed; quarterly trigger-inventory review tasks fire to the Data Privacy Steward

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Notice versions, approval records, per-channel delivery logs and re-notice campaigns retained 10 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any collection trigger found operating without notice delivery, and any stale version served, is logged as an exception with affected-record counts and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Privacy Counsel signs the remediation of every notice-gap exception, including whether corrective notice to affected individuals is required

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The trigger-point inventory, all new policies and claims opened in the period, portal registrations, and the notice version and delivery logs across all channels

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if any trigger point lacks a delivery mechanism, any sampled collection shows no notice delivery at/before collection, or a superseded version was served after its retirement date; ≥1 systemic fail escalates to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven at every collection; verification test runs annually over the year's collection events across all channels

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Third-line review; the reviewer must not have drafted the notice or operated any tested delivery channel

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual privacy-notice verification workpaper (trigger reconciliation, delivery sampling per channel, content re-check, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Current notice with approval trail, trigger inventory and delivery-log extracts, presentable to the Privacy Commissioner (PrivCom) or BMA within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Privacy Officer owns PrivCom correspondence; Privacy Counsel clears responses; notice failures material to conduct also route to the Head of Compliance for BMA self-report assessment

checklist.step: Maintain the collection trigger-point inventory
actions: List every point where the insurer collects personal information: new-business applications, claims FNOL, portal registration, contact-centre calls, producer/broker submissions, marketing sign-ups and telematics/wearable feeds where used.
For each trigger record the channel, the system of record, the notice delivery mechanism and the delivery-log location.
Review the inventory quarterly against new product launches and process changes with the Business Analyst community.
Version the inventory and file each revision.
checklist.done: a quarterly-reviewed inventory maps every collection trigger to its delivery mechanism and log.

checklist.step: Map processing purposes to notice content
actions: Maintain the data-use register: each purpose (underwriting, claims handling, fraud prevention, reinsurance, marketing), the information types used, and the recipient categories (reinsurers, service providers, regulators).
Cross-check that every register purpose appears in the current notice text and flag any silent use immediately.
Feed register changes into the re-notice workflow before the new use goes live.
Reconcile register-to-notice quarterly.
checklist.done: every live processing purpose is reflected in the current notice, reconciled quarterly.

checklist.step: Draft the PIPA-compliant notice content
actions: Draft against the PIPA s.9 checklist: the fact and purposes of collection, types of personal information, recipient categories, the privacy officer's identity and contact details, and the individual's rights of access and correction.
Write in plain language, layered: short-form summary at the collection point linking to the full notice.
Cover sensitive-information handling (health data in underwriting and claims) explicitly.
Record the PIPA-section-to-paragraph mapping in the approval memo.
checklist.done: the draft covers every s.9 element with a documented section-to-paragraph mapping.

checklist.step: Approve and version-control each notice release
actions: Approve the notice jointly with Privacy Counsel and assign a version number and effective date.
Store the approved version in the document repository with its approval memo; mark the prior version retired with an end date.
Notify every channel owner of the new version and its go-live date with a 10-business-day implementation window.
Keep a public change summary so individuals can see what changed.
checklist.done: the approved version is live in the repository with effective/retirement dates and channel owners notified.

checklist.step: Publish the notice on the portal and website
actions: Publish the new version to the portal footer, the registration flow and the public website privacy page on the effective date.
Present the short-form notice with an acknowledgment checkpoint in the portal registration flow before account creation completes.
Verify the linked full notice renders the current version — check the version string on the page, not the CMS record.
Log each registration's notice version and acknowledgment timestamp.
checklist.done: the portal serves the current version at registration with logged, versioned acknowledgments.

checklist.step: Embed notice delivery in the new-business workflow
actions: Configure the policy admin platform to attach the current short-form notice to every application package and the full notice to the policy issuance pack.
Record the notice version and delivery timestamp on the policy record at application receipt.
Block issuance where the application package predates the collection of personal information without notice attachment, forcing corrective delivery first.
Regression-test the attachment logic after each platform release.
checklist.done: every application and issuance carries a logged, versioned notice delivery, enforced by the platform.

checklist.step: Deliver the notice at claims intake
actions: At FNOL, read the short privacy statement from the intake script for phone claims, or present the notice screen for digital FNOL, before collecting claim details beyond identification.
Record the delivery flag and notice version on the claim file at intake.
For third-party claimants, send the notice with the first written acknowledgment of the claim.
Route intake-script changes through the Privacy Officer before use.
checklist.done: every new claim shows a versioned notice-delivery flag at intake, third parties included.

checklist.step: Wire the contact centre script and IVR notice
actions: Configure the Genesys IVR to play the call-recording and privacy statement before an agent connects.
Keep the agent-facing short notice text in the desktop scripting for interactions collecting new personal information.
Log the IVR notice playback against the interaction record.
Verify the IVR message references the current notice version after each version release.
checklist.done: the IVR plays the current statement with playback logged, and agent scripts carry the short notice.

checklist.step: Distribute notice obligations through the producer channel
actions: Publish the current notice pack to the broker/agent portal with the effective date and an obligation banner on the new-business screens.
Include the notice-delivery obligation in producer agreements and the annual producer attestation.
Collect the producer's delivery confirmation flag with each submitted application.
Chase producers with missing confirmation flags monthly and report persistent offenders to the Producer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: producers access the current pack, contract to deliver it, and confirm delivery per application.

checklist.step: Log every delivery event with version and timestamp
actions: Consolidate delivery events from the policy admin, claims, portal, Genesys and producer channels into the privacy delivery log in the warehouse.
Standardise each event: individual identifier, trigger type, channel, notice version, timestamp.
Run the weekly completeness check comparing collection events to delivery events per channel and alert on gaps.
Retain the log per the retention schedule.
checklist.done: a consolidated, weekly-checked delivery log covers all channels with version and timestamp per event.

checklist.step: Trigger re-notice on any material change of use
actions: On any data-use register change adding a purpose or recipient category, assess whether existing individuals' information will be used in the new way.
Where it will, issue the re-notice (portal message, email, or policy-pack insert per channel preference) before the new use commences.
Record the re-notice campaign: population, channel, version, send date and delivery counts.
Hold the new processing until the campaign completes — the register workflow enforces the block.
checklist.done: no new use of existing information commences before a recorded re-notice campaign completes.

checklist.step: Check translation and accessibility of the notice
actions: Verify the notice meets plain-language and accessibility standards (screen-reader compatible web version, large-print available on request).
Produce translations where a material policyholder segment operates in another language, with Privacy Counsel certifying translation fidelity.
Review readability on each version release.
File accessibility check results with the version record.
checklist.done: each version passes accessibility review with certified translations where required.

checklist.step: Train frontline staff and producers on notice duties
actions: Maintain the notice-delivery module in the LMS covering triggers, scripts and logging duties per channel.
Assign to all intake, contact-centre and new-business staff at onboarding and annually; assign the producer variant through the producer portal.
Chase completion to 100% within 30 days of assignment, escalating through line managers.
Refresh the module within 20 business days of each notice version release.
checklist.done: training completion is at 100% or escalated, with content refreshed per version release.

checklist.step: Log and remediate notice-gap exceptions
actions: Log every trigger found operating without delivery, and every stale-version incident, as a GRC exception with the affected-record count and period.
With Privacy Counsel, decide whether corrective notice to affected individuals is required and execute it where so.
Fix the mechanical cause (broken attachment logic, missed channel) with a dated ticket.
Assess systemic gaps against the BMA self-report criteria with the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every gap is logged with affected counts, corrective notice decided, cause fixed and self-report assessed.

checklist.step: Retain notice versions and delivery evidence
actions: File every notice version with approval memo, effective/retirement dates and the s.9 mapping.
Archive periodic delivery-log extracts and re-notice campaign records.
Apply the 10-year retention label and verify retrieval by version and by individual identifier.
checklist.done: versions and delivery evidence are filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by version and individual.

testing.step: Build the period's collection-event population
actions: Extract from the warehouse all new-business applications, new claims, portal registrations and producer submissions for the period.
Extract the consolidated privacy delivery log for the same period.
Obtain the current trigger-point inventory and notice version register.
Sign the population with per-channel counts.
testing.done: signed per-channel collection and delivery extracts plus the inventory form the population.

testing.step: Reconcile the trigger inventory to the live process catalogue
actions: Compare the trigger inventory to the operating-model process catalogue and the period's product launches.
List collection-bearing processes absent from the inventory — each is a coverage exception.
Verify each inventory trigger names a working delivery mechanism and log location.
testing.done: the inventory covers every live collection process or gaps are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Sample new policies and verify notice delivery at collection
actions: Randomly select 25 new policies with a recorded seed, spread across direct and producer channels.
In the policy admin platform open each policy record and read the notice version and delivery timestamp at application receipt.
Confirm the delivery timestamp is at or before the personal-information collection timestamp.
A missing flag, or delivery after collection, is an exception.
testing.done: every sampled policy shows versioned delivery at or before collection.

testing.step: Sample claims and portal registrations the same way
actions: Select 15 claims and verify the intake delivery flag and version on each claim file, including at least 3 third-party claimants.
Select 15 portal registrations and verify the acknowledgment record and version in the portal log.
For 5 phone claims, pull the Genesys interaction records and confirm the IVR notice playback logged.
Missing flags or playbacks are exceptions.
testing.done: sampled claims, registrations and calls all show logged, versioned delivery events.

testing.step: Verify the served version matched the approved version over time
actions: Build the version timeline from the register: each version's effective and retirement dates.
For every sampled delivery event, check the served version was the approved one for that date.
Query the delivery log for any events citing a retired version after its retirement date plus the 10-day implementation window — each channel doing so is a systemic exception.
testing.done: all sampled events served the in-force version and no channel served retired versions past the window.

testing.step: Re-check the notice content against PIPA s.9
actions: Independently verify the current notice against each s.9 element: purposes, information types, recipients, privacy officer contact, individual rights.
Cross-check the data-use register for any live purpose absent from the notice text.
Confirm the privacy officer contact details published are current and reachable.
A silent purpose or missing element is an exception requiring a version release.
testing.done: the current notice independently satisfies every s.9 element with no silent purposes.

testing.step: Verify re-notice preceded any new use
actions: List the period's data-use register changes that added purposes or recipients.
For each, locate the re-notice campaign record and compare its completion date to the new use's go-live date.
A new use commencing before campaign completion is an exception; verify the workflow block's audit trail to see whether it was overridden.
testing.done: every new use traces to a completed prior re-notice, with any override exposed.

testing.step: Test producer-channel delivery confirmations
actions: For the producer-submitted applications in the sample, verify the producer delivery-confirmation flag accompanied each submission.
Check the monthly missing-flag chase reports exist and persistent offenders reached the Producer Compliance Manager.
Confirm the portal served the current notice pack during the period via its content history.
testing.done: producer submissions carry confirmations, chases are evidenced, and the portal pack was current.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a ticket per exception citing the trigger, channel and affected-record estimate.
Assign root cause (broken attachment logic, script drift, producer non-compliance, silent purpose) and a named owner.
Systemic gaps trigger the corrective-notice decision with Privacy Counsel and a BMA/PrivCom report assessment with the Head of Compliance.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has a ticket, root cause, owner, corrective-notice decision and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute per-channel exception rates against the delivery and version thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references.
Sign as independent reviewer, having drafted no notice and operated no tested channel.
Report to the Audit Committee and the Privacy Officer and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with per-channel rates, conclusion and reporting date is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: DPO owns the DSAR operation and its SLAs; refusals and exemption calls escalate to Privacy Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Bermuda PIPA (fully in force 1 January 2025) access and correction rights, read with Privacy Commissioner (PrivCom) guidance on response periods; re-verified at each procedure review and on any PrivCom guidance update

In-scope processes.value: End-to-end handling of data-subject access, correction and erasure requests against the Bermuda insurer's records: intake across all channels, identity verification, 14-day acknowledgment, multi-system search, exemption review, and delivery within the 45-day statutory response period

In-scope systems.value: DSAR case management with clock tracking in the workflow tool; searches span the policy admin platform, claims platform, data warehouse and document repositories; delivery via secure portal message

Compliance procedure documented.value: DSAR Handling Procedure — intake channels, identity-verification tiers, clock rules (received date starts day 0; acknowledge within 14 days; respond within 45 days; one documented extension with written notice), search scope matrix, exemption checklist and secure-delivery steps

Compliance procedure approved.value: Procedure approved by the DPO and Privacy Counsel; re-approved on any PIPA amendment or PrivCom guidance change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per request: acknowledgment within 14 days of receipt; substantive response within 45 days; extension notice, where genuinely needed, issued in writing before day 45 with the reason and new date

Deadline reminders configured.value: The case tool starts the clock on the logged received date and fires alerts at day 7 (acknowledgment), day 30 and day 40 to the assigned handler and the DPO; breached clocks page the Privacy Officer

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: DSAR case files (request, ID verification, search records, exemption notes, response and delivery proof) retained 10 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Late acknowledgments, late responses, and searches that missed a system of record are logged as exceptions with root cause and disposition; patterns report to PrivCom-facing management review

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Privacy Counsel signs every refusal, every exemption applied, and the remediation of every late-response exception

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every DSAR received in the period across all intake channels (web form, privacy mailbox, post, phone, in-person via agents), reconciled to channel receipts

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if any sampled request missed the 14-day acknowledgment or 45-day response without a compliant pre-deadline extension, lacked ID verification, or skipped a system in the search matrix; ≥1 fail escalates to the DPO and Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven per request; verification test runs annually over the full year's DSAR log, with a semi-annual mini-test if volumes exceed 50 per quarter

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Third-line review; the reviewer must not have handled any sampled request or approved any sampled exemption

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual DSAR verification workpaper (channel reconciliation, clock recomputation, search re-performance, exemption review, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: DSAR log with per-request clock evidence and the procedure, presentable to the Privacy Commissioner within 5 business days of an inquiry or complaint investigation

Regulator response path.value: DPO owns PrivCom complaint and inquiry responses; Privacy Counsel clears every submission; conduct-relevant failures also route to the Head of Compliance for BMA self-report assessment

checklist.step: Operate every DSAR intake channel
actions: Maintain the portal request form, the published privacy mailbox, the postal address and the phone script as live intake channels, all referenced in the privacy notice.
Brief contact-centre and agency staff to recognise an access or correction request in any wording and forward it to the privacy mailbox the same day.
Check each channel weekly for stranded requests (spam folders, unmonitored queues).
Record the channel on every logged request.
checklist.done: all published channels are live, staff forward same-day, and weekly channel sweeps are logged.

checklist.step: Log every request and start the clock at receipt
actions: Create the case in the workflow tool the day the request arrives, recording the received date as day 0 — the date it hit any company channel, not the date privacy saw it.
Classify the request type: access, correction, erasure, or mixed.
Verify the clock alerts armed: day-7 acknowledgment warning, day-30 and day-40 response warnings to the handler and DPO.
Assign a named handler within 1 business day.
checklist.done: every request is a same-day case with day 0 at channel receipt, typed, alarmed and assigned.

checklist.step: Verify the requester's identity proportionately
actions: Apply the tiered verification standard: portal-authenticated customers are already verified; postal/email requesters provide policy number plus one government-ID match; authorised representatives provide the signed authority.
Never demand more identification than needed — excessive friction is itself a PIPA compliance risk; record the tier applied.
Pause the substantive clock only per the procedure's rules while awaiting ID, and document the pause dates in the case.
Reject impersonation attempts and log them to the fraud referral path.
checklist.done: every case records the verification tier, evidence and any documented clock pause.

checklist.step: Acknowledge the request within 14 days
actions: Send the acknowledgment within 14 days of receipt: confirm the request as understood, state the expected response date, and name the contact.
Where scope is ambiguous, use the acknowledgment to confirm scope — ask a clarifying question without stopping work on the unambiguous part.
Log the sent acknowledgment and its date in the case.
The day-7 alert escalates any unacknowledged case to the DPO.
checklist.done: every case shows an acknowledgment sent within 14 days with scope confirmed or queried.

checklist.step: Scope the search across every system holding the individual's data
actions: Apply the search-scope matrix: policy admin platform, claims platform, billing, the data warehouse, document repositories, call recordings in Genesys, and email where the request reasonably reaches it.
Resolve the individual's identifiers (policy numbers, claim numbers, party ids) via the warehouse party-match before searching, so aliases are not missed.
Record each system searched, the query used, the searcher and the date on the case's search log.
Confirm any deliberate scope exclusion with the DPO in writing on the case.
checklist.done: the case search log shows every matrix system searched with queries, dates and any authorised exclusions.

checklist.step: Compile the response package
actions: Assemble the personal information found into the response template: data items grouped by system, purposes of use, recipient categories and retention periods.
Convert to a readable format — no raw table dumps without field explanations.
Note items withheld pending the exemption review so nothing silently disappears.
Stage the package for QA at least 10 days before the response deadline.
checklist.done: a readable, complete package with withheld items flagged is staged 10 days before deadline.

checklist.step: Apply exemptions and third-party redactions with counsel
actions: Review every proposed withholding against PIPA's exemptions: third-party personal information, legal privilege, and information whose disclosure the Act excepts.
Redact third-party identities in claims and complaint records rather than withholding whole documents where severance is practicable.
Record each exemption applied, the PIPA basis, and the balancing rationale on the case.
Sign the exemption schedule — no withholding stands without counsel signature.
checklist.done: every withholding carries a counsel-signed PIPA basis with severance preferred over blanket refusal.

checklist.step: QA the response before release
actions: Check the package against the search log — every searched system's findings either appear or sit on the signed exemption schedule.
Verify no other individual's unredacted data is included — misdelivery is itself a breach.
Confirm the response letter states the individual's correction rights and the PrivCom complaint route.
Sign the QA record on the case.
checklist.done: the DPO's signed QA confirms completeness, clean redaction and required rights wording.

checklist.step: Deliver the response securely within 45 days
actions: Deliver via secure portal message for portal users, or password-protected file with the password sent by a second channel for others.
Send by the day-45 deadline computed from the received date, less any documented ID-verification pause.
Log the delivery method, date and proof (portal read receipt, dispatch record) on the case.
Close the case only after delivery proof is attached.
checklist.done: delivery proof within the computed deadline is attached and the case closed on it.

checklist.step: Execute corrections and erasures in the source systems
actions: For upheld correction requests, amend the record in the system of record (policy admin, claims or billing) — not just the warehouse copy — and let downstream syncs propagate.
For erasure requests, apply the retention-schedule test with the DPO: erase what no legal basis retains, and document what insurance-law retention requires keeping and why.
Confirm the change landed by re-querying after the sync cycle.
Notify the requester of the outcome, including any retained items and their basis.
checklist.done: corrections landed in source systems, erasure decisions are retention-tested, and the requester is told the outcome.

checklist.step: Handle extensions with written notice before the deadline
actions: Permit an extension only for genuine complexity or volume, decided by the DPO — never for queue backlog.
Send the written extension notice before day 45 stating the reason and the new committed date.
Log the notice and re-arm the clock alerts against the new date.
Track extension frequency monthly — a rising rate is a capacity problem, not a legal remedy.
checklist.done: every extension shows a pre-deadline written notice with reason and new date, and rates are tracked.

checklist.step: Issue refusals with reasons and the complaint route
actions: Where a request is refused in whole (identity unverifiable, manifestly unfounded per the procedure's tests), draft the refusal stating the ground and the PIPA basis.
Include the individual's right to complain to the Privacy Commissioner and PrivCom's contact details.
Sign the refusal and log it distinctly in the DSAR log for pattern monitoring.
Report refusal counts to the DPO quarterly.
checklist.done: every refusal is counsel-signed with grounds and the PrivCom route, and counts are monitored.

checklist.step: Publish the monthly DSAR SLA dashboard
actions: Compile monthly: requests received by channel and type, acknowledgment timeliness, response timeliness, extensions, refusals and open-case ageing.
Mark SLA attainment against the 14-day and 45-day clocks and trend it.
Review with the DPO and agree actions on any deteriorating metric.
File each month's dashboard in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a monthly dashboard with clock attainment and agreed actions is reviewed and filed.

checklist.step: Log and remediate SLA and scope exceptions
actions: Log every late acknowledgment, late response and missed-system search as a GRC exception with the case reference.
Assign root cause (channel sweep failure, search matrix gap, capacity) and a dated fix.
Where a late response coincides with a PrivCom complaint, prepare the response file with Privacy Counsel proactively.
Obtain Privacy Counsel sign-off on each exception's closure.
checklist.done: every SLA or scope failure is a logged exception with root cause, dated fix and counsel-signed closure.

checklist.step: Retain DSAR case files
actions: Archive each closed case: request, ID evidence, search log, exemption schedule, QA record, response and delivery proof.
Apply the 10-year retention label.
Verify quarterly that a sampled closed case retrieves end-to-end by case id.
checklist.done: closed cases archive complete, retention-labelled and pass the quarterly retrieval check.

testing.step: Build the period's DSAR population from all channels
actions: Extract the full DSAR log from the case tool for the period with received, acknowledged, responded and closed dates.
Independently pull the portal form submissions and privacy-mailbox message list for the same period.
Sign the population with counts by channel and type.
testing.done: the case-log extract and independent channel pulls are signed as the population.

testing.step: Reconcile channel receipts to logged cases
actions: Match every portal submission and mailbox request to a case; an unlogged request is an automatic fail with its own clock exposure.
Check the logged received date equals the channel receipt date — day 0 shifted to privacy-team pickup is a clock manipulation exception.
Sample 5 contact-centre interactions tagged as rights requests and confirm each was forwarded and logged same-day.
testing.done: every channel receipt traces to a case with an honest day 0, or is logged as a fail.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of refusals, extensions and erasure requests.
Randomly select 25 further cases with a recorded seed, spread across channels and request types; minimum 30 cases total.
Record seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all refusals, extensions and erasures plus random cases exists.

testing.step: Recompute the acknowledgment and response clocks
actions: For each sampled case, recompute days from the channel receipt date to the acknowledgment (≤14) and to the delivered response (≤45), honouring only documented ID-verification pauses.
Verify any extension shows a written notice sent before day 45 with reason and new date, and the response met the new date.
Compare recomputed figures to the dashboard's reported attainment; a discrepancy is its own exception.
Late clocks without compliant extensions are fails.
testing.done: every sampled case recomputes within clock or carries a compliant extension, and the dashboard reconciles.

testing.step: Verify identity-verification evidence
actions: Check each sampled case records the verification tier and holds the matching evidence.
Confirm representative-submitted requests hold the signed authority.
Check any clock pause for ID matches the documented request-and-receipt dates, not a retrofitted excuse.
A response released without verification evidence is a fail and a potential misdelivery incident.
testing.done: every sampled case shows tiered verification evidence with honest pause documentation.

testing.step: Re-perform the search scope on sampled cases
actions: For 10 sampled cases, resolve the individual's identifiers through the warehouse party-match and list which matrix systems hold their data.
Compare to the case's search log; a system holding data but never searched is an exception.
Re-run one search query per case and compare result counts to the compiled package for material omissions.
Check deliberate exclusions carry the DPO's written authorisation.
testing.done: sampled search logs cover every system actually holding the individual's data, verified by re-query.

testing.step: Review exemptions, redactions and refusals
actions: Independently review each sampled exemption schedule: is the PIPA basis correct and the balancing rationale supportable?
Inspect sampled redacted documents to confirm severance was used where practicable rather than blanket withholding.
Re-read each refusal for valid grounds and the PrivCom complaint wording.
An unsigned or unsupportable withholding is an exception; reviewer must not have signed the original.
testing.done: sampled withholdings and refusals stand up to independent counsel review with signatures present.

testing.step: Verify corrections and erasures landed in source systems
actions: For every sampled correction, query the system of record and confirm the amended value is live, not just marked done in the case tool.
For every sampled erasure, confirm erased items are gone and each retained item carries a documented retention basis.
Confirm the requester-outcome letter matches what actually happened in the systems.
A 'completed' correction absent from the source system is a fail.
testing.done: sampled corrections and erasures are proven in the source systems and match the outcome letters.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a ticket per exception citing the case id and the clock, scope or evidence failure.
Assign root cause (unlogged channel, shifted day 0, matrix gap, capacity) and a named owner.
Misdelivery or unverified-release findings open an incident and a PIPA breach assessment with the DPO immediately.
Carry open exceptions into the next test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has a ticket, root cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute exception rates against the clock, verification and search-scope thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references.
Sign as independent reviewer, having handled no sampled request and signed no sampled exemption.
Report to the Audit Committee and the DPO and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with conclusion, exception rates and reporting date is filed.
